9187 bahú 'much, many, great' RV., bahuka - 'costing much' lex. [√ baṁh ] Pa. bahu -, °uka - 'much', Aś. bahu n. sg. 'much', bahuka - 'large'; NiDoc. bahu sg. and pl., bahuv́e pl.
'much, many', Pk. bahu -, °uga -, °ū̆a -, °uaya -; Gy. eur. buhu 'much', arm. buhu 'large, much, very', as. (Baluči) bahu ; Paš.lauṛ. bū , dar. weg. chil. bō ( h ) 'many', Shum. bō , Kal.rumb. boʰ ; Kho. bo ( h ) 'much, many'; S. ḇahū̃ 'much' (< bahukam ); L. (Ju.) ḇahū̃ , bahū̃ 'much,
many, great', awāṇ. bàū̃ , P. bahu , bahũ , A. B. Or. Mth.
G. bahu ; OM. bauhā 'much', Ko. bhav , bho ; Si. bohō , bō 'much, many' ( bosō learned spelling for bohō ; buhu ← Pa. H.Smith JA 1950, 186). bahutithá-, bahutva-, bahudhā́, bahura-, bahulá-;
bahukāra-, bahumāna-, bahurūpá-, bahuvāra -. Addenda: bahú-: Kho. bo 'much, very' BKhoT 66. † bahutara -.

28 ákṣata 'unhurt' RV., 'not crushed' ĀśvGr̥., m. pl. 'uncrushed barley' Kālid. [ kṣatá -¹] Pa. akkhata - 'unhurt'; Pk. akkhaya - 'unhurt, unbroken',
m. pl. 'uncrushed rice'; S. akho m. 'offering of
grain thrown into water or given to mendicants'; Ku. ã̄khat 'rice soaked in water and used for religious purposes'
(X lw. Sk.); A. ākhai 'parched paddy, husked maize'; G. ākhũ 'whole, uncastrated', ākhlɔ m. 'uncastrated bull', ākhī f. 'ceremony of carrying rice or corn in the hand
round a person to remove the effects of the evil eye';
M. ā̆khā 'whole, undivided'; Ko. ākho , āko 'complete'. Addenda: ákṣata-: S.kcch. ã̄kho m. 'bull'.
